name: client and browser
owns: the code that runs on the other side: DOM, JavaScript engines, WebAssembly, service workers, extensions, embedded webviews and desktop shells
why_in_D: Half of the web attack surface is on the client, and it is the half defenders control least. The browser is the enforcement point for the same origin policy, so how the browser decides what is same origin decides what any stored script can reach. An extension runs with more privilege than the page it sits in. A webview is a browser with the policy stripped out.

factors.name: origin definition for the scheme in use
factors.def: which components form an origin for http, blob, data, filesystem and custom schemes
factors.observable: cross-context access permitted between two origins the browser treats as equal

factors.name: site versus origin distinction
factors.def: which protections key on registrable site and which on origin, and the registrable domain list used
factors.observable: a cross-subdomain access permitted by a site-scoped control

factors.name: scripts served without nosniff
factors.def: whether a resource can be interpreted as a script despite its declared type
factors.observable: a text or image response executing as script in an old engine

factors.name: DOM parser context switching
factors.def: whether the parser switches to a script-executing state for some elements regardless of insertion path
factors.observable: script execution from an insertion the developer considered inert

factors.name: inline script policy

factors.name: trusted types enforcement point
factors.def: whether sinks are guarded by the browser and which sinks are omitted
factors.observable: a string reaching a sink the policy does not cover

factors.name: sink inventory per browser engine
factors.def: which DOM properties and functions execute code, and where engines disagree
factors.observable: a sink that executes in one engine and not another

factors.name: prototype pollution reachability

factors.observable: property inherited by unrelated objects after a payload

factors.name: prototype pollution to gadget conversion
factors.def: whether a polluted property changes behaviour somewhere privileged, which is what turns it into impact
factors.observable: a privileged action triggered by an inherited property

factors.name: DOM clobbering surface

factors.name: postMessage origin validation

factors.name: frame ancestor policy coverage

factors.name: frame busting script dependence

factors.name: window opener relationship
factors.def: whether a new context can reach the opener and navigate it
factors.observable: navigation of a parent from a child context

factors.name: cross origin opener policy
factors.def: the isolation state that decides whether a popup shares a browsing context group
factors.observable: opener availability under narrow isolation

factors.name: fetch credentials default
factors.def: whether a cross-origin fetch includes credentials by default, which decides ambient authority

factors.name: simple request criteria
factors.def: which requests skip preflight, which decides whether a cross origin write needs cooperation
factors.observable: a write performed without a preflight

factors.name: preflight response caching

factors.name: credentialed wildcard handling

factors.name: service worker scope

factors.name: service worker persistence

factors.name: cache storage origin scoping
factors.def: whether cached responses are readable by any script on the origin, including an injected one
factors.observable: cached content read by a script that did not write it

factors.name: worker update semantics

factors.observable: behaviour of an unregistered worker after reload

factors.name: app cache and back-forward cache content

factors.name: history and URL state leakage

factors.name: CSS injection to exfiltration

factors.observable: a request triggered by a CSS selector matching a secret

factors.name: CSS cascade impact on UI
factors.def: whether injected style can hide or overlay controls, which is a UI redress primitive
factors.observable: a click landing on a different control than the one displayed

factors.name: font and image loading side channels
factors.def: whether resource loading can be used as an oracle for content the script cannot read

factors.name: performance API timing detail

factors.name: extension content script injection scope

factors.name: extension web accessible resources

factors.name: extension permission breadth

factors.name: webview JavaScript bridge exposure

factors.observable: a native method callable from page script

factors.name: webview file and content access

factors.name: webview navigation policy

factors.name: deep link and intent trust

factors.name: custom protocol handler registration

factors.name: electron fuse state

factors.name: asar integrity enforcement
factors.def: whether packaged application bytes are verified at load

factors.name: flutter web renderer differences

factors.name: react native web bridge differences

factors.name: webassembly import surface

factors.name: webassembly memory sharing across workers

factors.name: browser extension and page CSP interaction

factors.name: clipboard and permission prompt handling

factors.name: notification and payment API abuse

factors.name: file system access API scope

factors.observable: a handle usable after the session that granted it

factors.name: drag and drop data smuggling

factors.name: autofill and credential exposure

factors.name: headless and automation signals

factors.name: fingerprint surface breadth
factors.def: how many independent properties identify a client, which decides whether an identity can be held across sessions
